t: Section 110(e)(2) of the Veterans’ Health Care Act of 1984 (Public Law 98–528; 38 U.S.C. 1712A note) is amended by striking “through 2012” and inserting “through 2016”.

fable.w: This section only extends a date in an existing provision of the Veterans' Health Care Act of 1984 from 2012 to 2016. The tempting reading is that the amended provision might involve a committee or consultation, but nothing in the text itself brings any party outside the federal government into a federal decision, and the underlying provision appears to concern reports to Congress, which stay inside the government. There is no comment period, hearing, non-federal advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: is amended by striking “through 2012” and inserting “through 2016”

opus.w: This amendment only pushes an end date from 2012 to 2016. It sets up no process that brings people outside the federal government into a federal decision: no public comment, hearing, outside advisory panel, consultation with states or tribes, or right to sue. As I recall, the underlying provision concerns an internal VA committee and reports that go to Congress, and both of those stay inside the federal government. So the appearance of a committee does not make this participation.
opus.s: is amended by striking “through 2012” and inserting “through 2016”
opus.b:
1. **The tempting reading:** Section 110 of the Veterans' Health Care Act of 1984 deals with a VA special committee on post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), so extending it might look like extending an advisory body. As I recall the underlying law (the text here doesn't say), that committee is made up of VA staff, and subsection (e) covers its annual reports, which end up going to Congress. On the text in front of us, this amendment only changes an end date. It creates no outside consultation, hearing, comment period, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that extends a date limit in a previous statute. It does not create any mechanism for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a legislative adjustment of a timeframe.
qwen_chat.s: Section 110(e)(2) of the Veterans’ Health Care Act of 1984 (Public Law 98–528; 38 U.S.C. 1712A note) is amended by striking “through 2012” and inserting “through 2016”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the date extends a program that involves veterans, thus affecting their participation. However, the text itself is merely a technical amendment to a date limit in a previous statute. It does not establish any new process for consultation, comment, or interaction with outside parties. It is a legislative housekeeping provision.
